wy_solucious_secondus.blurb: The biggest boulder in the Cabin Boulders group, near the top of Sinks Canyon outside Lander at roughly 7,200 feet. Problems start on every side of the rock, so there is always a face in sun or shade. Expect slabs, traverses, aretes and a few overhanging lines on dense gneiss that rewards crimps and slopers. Of the eleven problems, around half are easy V1s, a few sit at V3 to V4, and one long traverse stands out at V7. It suits a short, pumpy session, and it is a handy stop to pair with the neighbouring blocks a short walk up the trail.

wy_3_mcflatus_roof_area.blurb: One of the four sections of Hoback Shield, a slabby limestone escarpment in Hoback Canyon south of Jackson. This group is a set of eleven bolted sport lines, each finishing under a sizeable roof. The grades are friendly for most intermediate climbers: four around 5.9, five in the 5.10 range, and two at 5.11. Climbing is sporty and pumpy, with pinches, dimples and a roof pull to finish, and a couple of the moderate lines are polished from traffic. The wider cliff faces south, so spring and fall are the comfortable seasons, with sun arriving by late morning in summer.

wy_cobra_the.blurb: A sport sector at Lake Point, the highest developed crag in Ten Sleep Canyon, centred on a free-standing pillar that curls around on itself. Lake Point's limestone is tighter than at many canyon crags, with widely spaced jugs on a mix of angles. The eleven routes lean hard: one climb in the 5.8 range, a couple of 5.10s, four at 5.11, then a 5.12 and three 5.13s. That makes it a better pick for strong 5.11 climbers and up than for beginners. Trees filter the afternoon light at the crag overall, and the pillar is a striking place to tick a few quality pitches.

wy_dream_land.blurb: A sport sector in the upper canyon part of Mondo Beyondo, Ten Sleep, running to the right where the Slavery Wall ends. It holds eleven bolted lines on dolomite with a wide span of difficulty, from an easy 5.7 and a 5.8 through two 5.10s to a core of six 5.11s and one 5.12. A few of the lines are among the best-rated at the whole crag, and the 5.10 Beer Bong is a well known classic that many visitors to the canyon try. A good spot for climbers working in the 5.10 and 5.11 range who want several quality routes close together.

wy_hot_lixx_family_fun_center.blurb: A compact sport wall in the upper canyon section of Mondo Beyondo, Ten Sleep. The middle of the cliff shows a horizontal split with a rounded bulge above it. Eleven bolted routes on dolomite are mostly short and pocketed, and they have a reputation for packing a lot of climbing into a modest height. Grades cluster in the 5.11 range: seven of them, with two at 5.10 and two at 5.12, so this is a wall for climbers who already lead the low 5.10s and want steady, sustained pitches rather than warm-ups.

wy_lankin_dome.blurb: A big granite dome in the Sweetwater Rocks of central Wyoming, at around 8,000 feet and in plain view from the road linking Jeffrey City and Muddy Gap. The rock is excellent reddish granite in slabs and exfoliated sheets, and the routes are long, mostly traditional multi-pitch lines with one bolted exception. Eleven climbs run from a fourth-class scramble through the 5.6 to 5.9 range, up to a few 5.11s. The south side is usually sunny, and the place is very quiet and can be wind-blasted. Bring a full rack, plenty of water and self-reliance, since there is nothing nearby.

wy_nfsr_121_a_k_a_phone_booth_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of boulders beside Highway 14A in the Eastern Big Horns, at roughly 9,200 feet on the range's western slope. The nickname comes from the unusually good phone signal here. Eleven problems run from V0 to V4, with an even spread of easy to moderate lines, so it works well for beginners and for a quick roadside stop with a few pads. The stone is a little crumbly in places but still gives enjoyable pinch-and-crimp moves. The boulders see sun most of the day, summer highs stay mild, and you may share the area with campers and families.
